clue.text: Cook, oriental, sought by 22 across in 3

annotationWithheld.why: Cook, oriental, sought by 22 across in 3 (4): E is oriental and the definition is Dorothy's goal, but no reading of 'Cook' gives HOM, so the wordplay cannot be shown honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: Cook, oriental, sought by 22 across in 3

clue.text: Land father in a modern art venue

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for father within the other pieces, between A and the gallery

parts.note: the ICA, the Institute of Contemporary Arts, is a London gallery for modern art
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A priest lands a place in a London gallery of contemporary art.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is a continent, a land mass, so it is an example of a land.

clue.text: Classic feature of western comic's non-Pommy equivalent, it's said

definitions.meaning: a feature is a feature film, and this 1939 musical is a classic of the cinema

definitions.text: western comic's non-Pommy equivalent, it's said
definitions.meaning: The Wizard of Id is an American comic strip; swap the Id for Oz, the colloquial name for Australia, a land of people who are not Poms, and the title is what you get

explanation.surface: Someone is comparing a Western comic strip with its supposed Australian counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: THE WIZARD OF ID is a long-running American comic strip. 'Pommy' is Australian slang for British; Oz is the casual name for Australia, so the non-British version swaps Id for Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: The film made from Baum's story is a much-loved musical picture, a classic feature film of 1939.

clue.text: Time Magazine edition's absorbing stuff

parts.note: an issue is one edition of a magazine

explanation.surface: An edition of Time magazine is gripping reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time Magazine' looks like the American weekly, but Time is just T and the magazine edition is an ISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue paper is soft material used to soak up spills, so it is absorbent stuff.

clue.text: Potential beef spread abroad?

parts.note: a cattle ranch in Spanish-speaking countries is a spread where future beef grazes, abroad rather than at home

explanation.surface: A rumour of a beef sandwich filling being exported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' suggests something on bread, but in ranching a spread is a large farm; cattle on it are beef to come.
explanation.definitionFit: An estancia is a large cattle estate in South America, a ranch raising animals for beef.

clue.text: Head of Bury United sought by 22 across's 25?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of Bury

parts.note: people united are as one

explanation.surface: The manager of Bury United football club is being chased by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is an English town with a football club, so Bury United reads as a team. Dorothy's dog, 25 down, would seek a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog famously goes looking for something to chew on, so Dorothy's pet would seek this object.

clue.text: Blimey! Again, sadly, without Britten opera

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the scrambled letters go around the exclamation
sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of Again are rearranged

parts.note: Lor is a dated exclamation of surprise, like Blimey

explanation.surface: Someone groans that a Britten opera is missing, again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means 'outside', an old sense; 'Blimey' is a British exclamation of surprise and so is LOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloriana is Benjamin Britten's opera about Elizabeth I, written for the 1953 coronation.

clue.text: Throw upstart of seventeen on seat

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of seventeen

parts.note: a pew is a bench seat in a church

explanation.surface: An upstart aged seventeen is thrown on to a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'Throw upstart', but the split is 'Throw up' and 'start of seventeen'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit, which is to throw up.

clue.text: Extremes of bad taste, not to be gone into

parts.note: food that tastes bad has gone off
limits are the outer extremes or boundaries

explanation.surface: Things in the very worst taste should be avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad taste' together means OFF, as food that tastes bad has gone off; the clue gives the extremes first, so 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbidden area is out of bounds, a place one must not enter.

clue.text: Primula — it's at the wrong beastly end for soup-making

parts.note: an ox is a beast of the farm
the lip is at the front end of an ox, the opposite end to the tail that makes soup

explanation.surface: A primrose seems to be the wrong part of an animal for making soup.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on oxtail soup: soup comes from the tail end of the ox, so the lip is at the wrong end.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild flower of the primrose genus, Primula.

clue.text: Man relocated from American plant

indicators.note: relocated means the remaining letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word American, from which the three of Man are removed; that the remaining letters also run in order inside it is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A man moves away from an American plant or factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of MAN from AMERICAN, leaving AERIC, and 'relocated' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Start to boast of part in 3

parts.note: a start is a sudden fright, a scare
to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone is told to begin bragging about a role in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' looks like an instruction to take a first letter, but Start is a noun meaning a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scarecrow is one of Dorothy's companions in the Oz story, a character part in it.

clue.text: Fungus grower's support to end

parts.note: to bear is to support a weight
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: Something holding up a mushroom farmer is about to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fungus' is jocular slang for facial hair, so a fungus grower is someone with a beard, not a mushroom farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beardie is an informal name for a bearded man, one who grows facial hair.

clue.text: Bishop Bucket sought by 12 in 3

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to bucket is to rain heavily

explanation.surface: A bishop named Bucket is wanted by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucket' looks like a name or a pail, but it is the verb for heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scarecrow in the Oz story wants a mind, so he seeks this organ of thought.

clue.text: Cannes' opener: "Times We Live In" sought by 24 down in 3

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, here of Cannes

parts.note: the times we live in are our age, the present era

explanation.surface: A film called Times We Live In opens the Cannes festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a film festival premiere; Cannes gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowardly Lion in the Oz story wants bravery, so he seeks this quality.

clue.text: Not published abroad, as New York Tribune is

definitions.meaning: to herald is to proclaim widely, so something not spread abroad has not been announced
the newspaper's later title was the New York Herald Tribune, so the plain New York Tribune lacks Herald

explanation.surface: A newspaper is said to be unavailable outside its home country.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'abroad' means widely, as in 'spread abroad', not overseas. The second reading splits the answer as un-Herald-ed: the Tribune without Herald in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Unheralded means not announced or proclaimed beforehand, without publicity.

clue.text: Debut — make yours on solving this

definitions.meaning: a debut is a first appearance or arrival on stage
a prize puzzle asks solvers to send in their completed grid as a competition submission

explanation.surface: A first crossword, with an invitation to send it in once solved.
explanation.walkthrough: This was a Prize crossword, so the solver sends a completed grid to the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is a coming in, so a first appearance; it is also a competition submission.

clue.text: Reserved a scrubber with no expression of joy

indicators.note: with no means the cry of joy is taken away from the bath sponge

parts.note: a loofah is a rough sponge for scrubbing in the bath
ah is a cry of pleasure

explanation.surface: A cleaner without a smile keeps herself to herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrubber' suggests a cleaner, but it is the bath sponge; remove AH from LOOFAH to leave LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and cool in manner, which is how a reserved person behaves.

clue.text: Start to dip in to scoop out squids?

indicators.note: in puts the first letter of dip inside the scrambled letters
out signals the letters of to scoop are put out of order
the start to a word is its first letter, here of dip

explanation.surface: Instructions for dipping in a spoon and scooping out squid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TO SCOOP into OCTOPOS, and 'in' places D, the start of dip, inside it. The question mark admits octopods are relatives of squids, not squids.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopods are eight-armed cephalopods, close cousins of squid, so the query is fair.

clue.text: Ancient Everest pass leads back climber

indicators.note: back means the picked letters are read in the opposite direction
leads are the leading letters, the first of Ancient, Everest and pass

explanation.surface: An old route up Everest leads a mountaineer back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' takes A, E and P, and 'back' reverses AEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea plant climbs by tendrils, so it is a climber in the garden sense.

clue.text: Pinhole camera's top removed for a game

indicators.note: removed is read as re-moved, moved again, so the letters are shuffled
the top of a word is its first letter, here of camera

explanation.surface: The top of a pinhole camera has been taken off for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' looks like deletion, but it means re-moved: shuffle PINHOLE plus C.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinochle is a card game for two to four players using a doubled deck.

clue.text: Media mogul, no saint, sought by 23 in 3

indicators.note: no means the abbreviation for saint is left out of the name

parts.note: William Randolph Hearst was an American newspaper magnate

explanation.surface: A press baron, no saint, is pursued by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S from HEARST.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tin Man in the Oz story wants feeling, so he seeks this organ.

clue.text: Web community member not gross? One school of thought

parts.note: net is the amount after deductions, not gross
I is the Roman numeral for one
Zen is a school of Buddhist thought

explanation.surface: An internet user asks if they're not rude, citing a school of philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like 'disgusting', but it is the accounting sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A netizen is a citizen of the internet, an active user of online communities.

clue.text: Fish swallowing hot molten lead in 3

indicators.note: swallowing means the fish name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a dory is a sea fish

indicators.note: molten means melted down, so the letters of hot are reformed

explanation.surface: A fish gulps down hot molten metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the metal, but it means the leading role; 'molten' makes OTH from HOT, and 'swallowing' puts that inside the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy Gale is the heroine of the Oz story, the lead role.

clue.text: Hell might be appalling

definitions.note: the definition is read as a noun, the act of appalling, matching the noun dismay

parts.note: Dis is the god of the underworld, and the name for Hell
may means might be, expressing possibility

explanation.surface: Hell could prove appalling.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman underworld, and so a name for Hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is consternation, the feeling caused by something that shocks or appals.

clue.text: Outdated money piece seen in 3

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
a piece in chess or draughts is a man

explanation.surface: An old coin is on display.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN for money is dated slang; MAN is a playing piece, as in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tin Man is the metal woodsman among Dorothy's companions in the Oz story.

clue.text: Cheek and gums make-up? Yes and no

parts.note: lip is impudence, cheek
gums is glues, sticks

explanation.surface: Is it make-up for cheeks and gums? Partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek and gums' look like parts of the face, but mean LIP and STICKS. 'Yes and no' comments that these are make-up but not for cheeks or gums.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipsticks are cosmetics for colouring the lips, a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Millions, though not Lean, up for part in 3

indicators.note: though not means the letters that follow are taken out of the larger word

parts.note: the word Millions as written, from which the reversed letters are removed; that the remaining letters also run in order inside it is a coincidence

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the word for lean from bottom to top

parts.note: slim means lean, thin

explanation.surface: Millions are spent, though not by a lean director, on a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SLIM to MILS, and those letters are removed in order from MILLIONS. 'Lean' looks like the director David Lean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cowardly Lion is one of Dorothy's companions, a role in the Oz story.

clue.text: 3's pet character in this is entirely Latinised

definitions.meaning: Dorothy's little dog in the Oz film is a pet character
the Latin phrase in ... means entirely, so this word follows in

explanation.surface: A pet in a film whose name is wholly Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works by completing the Latin phrase meaning 'entirely, as a whole'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toto is Dorothy's cairn terrier in the Oz story.

clue.text: Like a beanpole put round two fertiliser elements

indicators.note: round means the word for put goes around the two chemical symbols

parts.note: to lay is to put down
N is nitrogen and K is potassium, two key elements in fertiliser

explanation.surface: Fertiliser is spread round a tall beanpole.
explanation.walkthrough: N, P and K are the elements in garden fertiliser; here N and K go inside LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanky means tall and thin, as a beanpole of a person is.

clue.text: Hairy beasts' gasses

explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Hairy beasts'' is plural; read the apostrophe as part of a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaks are shaggy Tibetan oxen, and to yak is to chatter, as to gas is.

clue.text: Hearsay broadcasting with Dee, say

parts.note: a programme that is broadcasting is on air

indicators.note: say signals that a word is spoken, and the French word meaning said sounds like Dee

parts.note: the river Dee, or the letter D spelt out

explanation.surface: Gossip on the radio with a presenter called Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means 'one says'; its second word is pronounced like 'Dee'.
explanation.definitionFit: An on dit is a piece of gossip, a rumour, which is hearsay.

clue.text: Property deal puts energy in Black Sea resort

indicators.note: in places the symbol for energy among the letters
resort is read as re-sort, sort again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A property transaction puts power into a Black Sea holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place, but read as re-sort it shuffles BLACK SEA plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaseback is a deal where property is sold and then leased back to the seller.
